Bayzat design task · Product concept

SyncAI

Where meeting conversations become clear decisions and accountable follow-up.

← All projectsMobile AI meeting assistant

PROJECT

SyncAI

SECTOR

AI · Workplace productivity

MY CONTRIBUTION

Mobile UX, UI and prototype

MOBILE PRODUCT DESIGN · BAYZAT DESIGN CHALLENGE

Where meetings turn into action.

I wanted SyncAI to help with the part of meetings that is easy to lose: what we agreed on, who is doing it and what happens next. I designed a mobile experience that brings the agenda, conversation and follow-up work together.

MY ROLEMobile UX, UI and prototype design
DELIVERABLESConnected screen flows · Light and dark themes
PROJECT STATUSDesign challenge / concept · Not a shipped service
Play the prototype ↗

01Why I designed it

The starting point was simple: a useful conversation still needs a clear next step. I wanted someone to leave a meeting knowing what had been decided, without having to piece it together from notes and messages.

I designed this for workplace teams, especially people organising regular meetings and the colleagues picking up tasks afterwards. That audience shaped the organisation setup, attendee mentions and individual and team task views. I would still need to test these assumptions with the people using it.

ORGANISER

Give the meeting a useful starting point.

I brought the meeting details and agenda together so the organiser has one place to start.

PARTICIPANT

Follow the discussion without losing commitments.

I wanted participants to be able to follow the discussion and quickly find the parts that need attention.

TEAM LEAD

See what needs to happen afterwards.

I made room for owners, deadlines and priorities so the follow-up is about actual work, rather than just another set of notes.

02What I worked on

I worked through the mobile journey from account setup and the home screen to agendas, meeting views, transcripts, summaries and tasks. I also designed the settings, reusable components and light and dark versions, then connected the main screens in Figma.

This was a Bayzat design challenge. My work here is the interface and prototype, rather than a live Bayzat product. The AI outputs, calls and integrations are designed scenarios, not working services.

03The meeting journey

01 / PREPARE

Build the agenda.

The organiser enters the meeting details and attendees, then prepares an agenda. I also included an AI draft and a way to generate another version.

02 / CAPTURE

Separate discussion from commitments.

Once the meeting starts, the transcript shows who said what and when. I used ACTION and DECISION labels to help people pick out commitments and agreements.

03 / FOLLOW THROUGH

Move into assigned work.

Afterwards, the summary brings the main points and proposed tasks together. Mine, Team and Completed views help people see their own work and the wider follow-up.

04A few decisions I made

PRIORITISATION

Start with the meeting that needs attention.

I put ongoing meetings and quick actions near the top of the home screen. I wanted the next useful action to be easy to find when someone opens the app.

INTERPRETATION

An action is different from a decision.

I kept actions and decisions separate because they mean different things. A decision is something the team agreed on; an action is work someone needs to do. I used text labels alongside colour to make that distinction clear.

OWNERSHIP

Keep the overview separate from the work.

I separated the meeting overview from the task list. Someone catching up needs the context, while someone following up needs to see the owner and priority of the work.

USER CONTROL

Let the assistant fit the routine.

I included reminders, quiet hours and summary preferences because an assistant should fit around someone’s working day. These are design choices I would test, rather than improvements I can claim to have measured.

05The rest of the experience

Find previous context

I included search and suggested queries so people have a way back into earlier meeting context. The full results and transcript-retrieval flow still needs work.

Connect existing tools

I explored connections to Google Calendar, Outlook, Zoom, Teams, Meet, Slack and Notion. The toggles show how those options could appear; the connection and authorisation flows are not implemented.

Support continued use

I also worked on account setup, organisation details, themes, support and feedback. These sit around the main meeting journey and help the concept feel like something people could return to.

06Where the prototype needs more work

I connected the main screens, but some important journeys still stop too early. The next pass needs to focus on what happens when someone creates a meeting, edits a summary or shares the follow-up.

DESIGNED

The core meeting journey.

The prototype shows how the meeting journey could work across the screens. I haven’t run participant usability tests or measured its effect on a team’s work.

TO COMPLETE

Finish the actions that deliver the promise.

I need to finish the meeting-creation success state, summary editing and sharing, search results and integration authorisation. These are the actions that carry the experience through to a useful result.

TO REFINE

Use mobile-native controls and consistent copy.

I would replace the hover-based task controls with taps for mobile. There are also copy fixes to make: the account-creation button says Sign In, and the summary-length section repeats Google Calendar text.

TO CLARIFY

Define the product boundary.

I need to make the product boundary clearer: does SyncAI host the meeting, or help with meetings on other platforms? The call controls and integration options need to tell one consistent story.

07What I would work on next

SOURCE

Show where a task came from.

I would let someone open the transcript passage behind a suggested task or decision. They should be able to check what was actually said.

REVIEW

Confirm the responsibility.

I would add a review step for the task wording, owner, deadline and priority. An AI suggestion should be easy to correct before anyone treats it as an agreed assignment.

CONSENT

Make recording and access explicit.

I would make recording consent and access visible: when capture is active, what is saved and who can read it. Those flows still need to be designed.

CONTINUITY

Carry unfinished work into the next meeting.

I would explore carrying unfinished tasks into the next meeting’s agenda. That could help the team pick up where it left off, but I would test whether it is useful before adding more complexity.

08How I would test it

  1. Find a decision. Ask a participant to locate a specific agreement in the transcript and summary. Observe navigation, interpretation and mistakes.
  2. Check an assignment. Give the participant an incorrectly inferred task owner or deadline. Test whether they recognise the error and can correct it before sharing.
  3. Complete the handover. Test the full path from meeting creation to a reviewed summary and confirmed task, including completion feedback.
  4. Understand consent. Check whether participants know when recording is active and who can access its outputs.

I would use these tests to find out where the flow is clear and where it breaks down. They are my next steps, not research I have already completed.

09What I took from this

For me, the useful part of SyncAI is the handover from talking about work to knowing what to do. The project gave me a way to work through that journey across mobile screens, AI-generated content and task views.

My next step would be to finish the review and confirmation flows, then put them in front of people. I want to find out whether they can check the record, spot a mistake and leave with a clear next action.
